item.description:
Clicker 0.3.3
- When macOS doesn't allow Clicker on the local network, Clicker now says so after the first attempt, instead of retrying and ending on "Couldn't connect". The notice explains where to turn it on, under Privacy & Security › Local Network, and has a button that opens Privacy & Security. - The remote is dimmed and can't be pressed until Clicker is connected to the Apple TV. Presses made while it was still connecting used to look like they worked, and were lost if the connection failed.

Clicker 0.3.2
- The device list now works from the keyboard like the Apps picker: Up and Down move the highlight and Return picks the TV. - While the device list is open, the remote's keys and trackpad swipes no longer reach the Apple TV behind it, and Space no longer picks a TV you didn't highlight. - Highlighted rows in the Apps picker and the device list use your accent color, so they're easy to read in Light mode. - Opening Settings with ⌘, closes an open popover first instead of carrying it along with the remote. - Rescan again tries the last known address of an Apple TV that was paired with an earlier version of Clicker.

Clicker 0.3.1
- The Apps picker's scroll bar no longer draws a dark track over the list on macOS 26 and later, and it now sits in the popover's margin instead of covering the favorite stars. - The device and Apps popovers follow a switch between Light and Dark mode, and Increase Contrast, while Clicker is running. - Clicker is now built against the macOS 27 SDK, so controls pick up the current system look.

Clicker 0.3.0
- Clicker now runs in the App Sandbox, so it can only reach the network and its own files. Your paired Apple TVs, favorite apps and settings carry over on the first launch.

Clicker 0.2.11
- New Invert Swipes setting in Settings › This Mac reverses the direction of two-finger trackpad swipes over the clickpad, for people who expect a swipe to scroll content rather than move the selection. - Quick trackpad swipes no longer sometimes jerk the selection back the wrong way at the end.

Clicker 0.2.10
- Holding a keyboard key now holds the button on the Apple TV, like holding a button on the remote: a held arrow keeps moving, and a held Return long-presses. - Fixed two Apple TVs with the same name and model, in different homes, unpairing each other when the Mac moved between networks.

Clicker 0.2.9
- When an update is available, a notice with an Update button now appears under the remote, in place of the dot on the menu bar icon. It shows even while the remote is unavailable, such as when the Apple TV is off. - Clicker no longer opens the update window on its own, including right after you log in. It waits until you click Update or Check for Updates…. - The connection error now names the Apple TV, for example "Couldn't connect to Living Room."

Clicker 0.2.8
- Pressing buttons while an Apple TV isn't responding no longer queues up long reconnect attempts that replay every press once it answers. Use Retry, or close and reopen the panel, to reconnect. - Re-identifying a paired Apple TV can no longer lose its pairing if saving fails partway.

Clicker 0.2.7
- Replies from the Apple TV are decoded correctly later in a session. After a few dozen commands, a decoding mistake could mix up repeated values in a reply, such as names in the app list. - Switching to another Apple TV while the previous one is still connecting no longer lets the old connection's events reach the remote.

Clicker 0.2.6
- Clicking Pair no longer briefly freezes the panel while the pairing keys are computed. - A connection that fails or is abandoned is cleaned up right away, so the next attempt actually reconnects instead of waiting out a timeout. - Quitting and closing the panel mid-connect no longer wait for a stalled Apple TV to time out. - Rescan no longer lets results from the previous search briefly change the device list.

Clicker 0.2.5
- Fixes the first button press after opening the panel sometimes doing nothing when the Apple TV had dropped the previous session. - Reconnects on its own a second after the Apple TV drops the session while the panel is open, and recovers from a stalled connection about twice as fast. - Tells the Apple TV the session is over when you quit, instead of leaving it with a dead connection. - Opening Clicker again while it's already running now shows the panel. - Shows the "Paired, but the pairing couldn't be saved" card when saving a pairing fails, instead of a remote that wouldn't connect. - After forgetting the selected Apple TV, switches to another one instead of waiting on the Choose card. - Esc now closes the device list first, and the list no longer reopens by itself the next time the panel opens. - A failed app launch no longer clears the Mute button's tint while the TV is still muted. - fn+Delete now removes the global shortcut while recording one. - Settings keeps "Last checked" up to date while it's open, and lists paired Apple TVs by name. - Keeps every past release in the update feed, so a Mac left behind by a future minimum macOS can still update to the last version it supports.

Clicker 0.2.4
- Simplifies the panel's buttons: the Power and ••• menu buttons no longer follow the system's menu tracking, so the rest of the panel stops re-rendering every time a menu closes.

Clicker 0.2.3
- Fixes the Back, TV, Play/Pause and Siri buttons blinking for a few frames when Settings was opened from the ••• menu.

Clicker 0.2.2
- The Shortcut row in Settings is a button that shows the chord: click it, press the keys, and it is set. Hover for the remove control, or press Delete while recording. Esc or a click elsewhere cancels. - The Name field is the standard text field again.

Clicker 0.2.1
- The Name and Shortcut fields in Settings look alike again. 0.2.0 drew the shortcut recorder as a filled capsule next to a rounded-rect Name field; both now share one surface.

Clicker 0.2.0
- A global keyboard shortcut opens or closes Clicker from any app. Record one in Settings › This Mac › Shortcut; it needs no Accessibility or Input Monitoring permission. - The panel hangs from the menu bar icon like a menu, and switching between the remote and Settings resizes it on one smooth curve. - Settings › This Mac explains the Name and Shortcut rows with info tooltips instead of a paragraph, and the login toggle is now called Open at Login, like System Settings. - Tooltips appear after a third of a second instead of about one second. - The homepage's download button links straight to the newest DMG.

Clicker 0.1.2
- Demo mode is compiled only into debug and --with-demo builds, so the released app no longer carries it. - Release workflow, site deployment and error handling improvements.
